title: A comprehensive protocol to study the effects of multilingualism on cognition and the brain in patients with progressive neurological diseases
author: Pliatsikas, Antoniou, et al.

steps.title: Configure online questionnaire system
steps.instruction: Host all questionnaires and behavioural tasks on the Gorilla platform; link any third‑party tools (e.g., Language History Questionnaire) via external URLs; this provides centralized, standardized data collection with minimal cost. Participating labs must cover participant recruitment and testing expenses.

steps.title: Acquire MRI sequences (≈40 min)
steps.instruction: In a 3 T scanner equipped with a 64‑channel head coil, run the following whole‑brain sequences:

substeps.instruction: Collect T1‑weighted MPRAGE 3D: 256 sagittal slices, 0.7 mm isotropic voxels, FOV 224 × 224 mm, TE 2.41 ms, TR 2400 ms, TI 1140 ms, flip angle 8°.
Collect 3D diffusion tensor imaging: 60 transverse slices, 2 mm isotropic voxels, FOV 260 × 260 mm, TE 70 ms, TR 1800 ms, two averages, 64 diffusion directions, b‑value 1000 s/mm².
Collect T2‑FLAIR: 192 slices, voxel size 0.4 × 0.4 × 0.9 mm, FOV 230 × 230 mm, TE 387 ms, TR 5000 ms, flip angle 120°, GRAPPA acceleration factor 2.
Collect resting‑state fMRI: 300 volumes, 68 transversal slices, voxel size 2.1 × 2.1 × 2.0 mm, FOV 192 × 192 mm, TE 30 ms, TR 1500 ms, flip angle 66°.

steps.title: Process MRI structural data
steps.instruction: Run the standard Freesurfer pipeline on the T1‑MPRAGE images to extract cortical thickness, surface‑area extent, and volume for grey‑matter regions defined by Freesurfer atlases.

steps.title: Process MRI diffusion data
steps.instruction: Using Freesurfer (or an equivalent diffusion toolbox), compute fractional anisotropy and mean diffusivity for individual white‑matter tracts from the DTI dataset.

steps.title: Process MRI FLAIR lesions
steps.instruction: Apply the Lesion Prediction Algorithm (LPA) via the Lesion Segmentation Tool v2.0.15 in SPM to the T2‑FLAIR images to detect, extract, and quantify white‑matter hyperintensities (number and volume) across the whole brain.

steps.title: Analyze resting‑state fMRI
steps.instruction: Feed the resting‑state fMRI data into FSL’s MELODIC pipeline; perform ICA to obtain independent components; select networks of interest (frontoparietal control, salience, default‑mode) based on the MELODIC atlas; average activity within each network for later modeling.

steps.title: Record resting‑state fNIRS (≈10 min)
steps.instruction: For participants incompatible with MRI, set up a portable fNIRS system (e.g., MediBrite) with a 27‑channel montage covering frontal and parietal regions bilaterally using the 10‑20 EEG layout. Use dual wavelengths (760 nm and 850 nm) at 75 Hz sampling. Place optodes 3 cm source‑detector apart and include 8 mm short‑separation channels. Have the participant keep eyes open and record 5 minutes of resting‑state activity.

steps.title: Preprocess fNIRS recordings
steps.instruction: Correct motion artefacts, apply a band‑pass filter (0.01–0.1 Hz), and perform physiological‑noise reduction on the raw HbO and HbR time series.

steps.title: Compute fNIRS connectivity
steps.instruction: Perform wavelet coherence analysis on the preprocessed HbO and HbR signals to assess inter‑ and intra‑hemispheric functional connectivity for each channel.

steps.title: Fit Generalised Additive Mixed Models
steps.instruction: Using maximal Generalised Additive Mixed Models, model each outcome separately: (i) cognitive accuracy and reaction times; (ii) regional grey‑matter thickness, surface area, volume and white‑matter FA/MD; (iii) number and volume of white‑matter lesions; (iv) averaged resting‑state fMRI network activity; (v) fNIRS HbO/HbR concentrations per channel. Include the multilingualism‑derived (MLD) score as the main predictor and covariates for lifestyle, quality of life, and mental health.
